16	The README and docs explain that Polyply can:
17	
18	- generate input files for polymer and biomacromolecule simulations;
19	- use user-specified building blocks or library polymers;
20	- generate coordinates with a multiscale random-walk workflow;
21	- tailor initial chain conformations through build files.

164	def compute_volume(block, coords, nonbond_params, treshold=1e-18):

167	    compute the radius of gyration taking into account
168	    the volume of each particle. The volume of a particle
169	    is considered to be the sigma value of it's LJ self-
170	    interaction parameter.

172	    Parameters
173	    ----------
174	    block:     :class:`vermouth.molecule.Block`
175	    coords:    dict[abc.hashable]
176	        dictionary of positions in from node_idx: np.array
177	    nonbond_params: dict[frozenset(abc.hashable, abc.hashable)]
178	        dictionary of nonbonded parameters with atom-types as
179	        keys and sigma, epsilon LJ parameters
180	    treshold: float
181	        distance from center of geometry at which the
182	        particle is not taken into account for the volume
183	        computation
184	
185	    Returns
186	    -------
187	    radius of gyration
188	    """
189	    n_atoms = len(coords)
190	    points = np.array(list(coords.values()))
191	    res_center_of_geometry = center_of_geometry(points)
192	    geom_vects = np.zeros((n_atoms, 3))
193	    idx = 0
194	    radii = []
195	    for node, coord in coords.items():
196	        atom_key = block.nodes[node]["atype"]
197	        rad = float(nonbond_params[frozenset([atom_key, atom_key])]["nb1"])
198	        diff = coord - res_center_of_geometry
199	        if np.linalg.norm(diff) > treshold:
200	            geom_vects[idx, :] = diff + u_vect(diff) * rad
201	            idx += 1

205	    # this can happen when multiple beads are stacked for
